'''Evgenia Andreevna Zabolotskaya''' (1935–2020) was a Russian-American physicist known for her contributions to [[nonlinear acoustics]].{{r|obit}} The ''Khokhlov–Zabolotskaya equation'' and the ''Khokhlov–Zabolotskaya–Kuznetsov equation'' in nonlinear acoustics are named in part for her.{{r|kz|kzk}}

==Education and career==
Zabolotskaya studied physics at [[Moscow State University]], earning her bachelor's degree<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Summer2020 |url=https://acousticstoday.org/issues/2020AT/Summer2020/files/basic-html/page87.html |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=acousticstoday.org}}</ref> and then later returning in 1968 to complete her PhD under the supervision of [[Rem Khokhlov]]. After working at the [[Andreyev Acoustics Institute]], she returned to Moscow State University in 1971, appointed to the biology department. In 1982, she moved again, to the {{ill|General Physics Institute|ru|Институт общей физики имени А. М. Прохорова РАН}} of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].{{r|silver}}

After meeting and beginning to work with [[University of Texas at Austin]] mechanical engineering professors David Blackstock and Mark Hamilton, starting in 1982, Zabolotskaya moved to the University of Texas in 1991. From 1997 to 2000 she was on leave from the university to work at a start-up company in Virginia. She retired in 2015.{{r|silver}}

She died on June 2, 2020, in [[Santa Fe, New Mexico]].{{r|obit}}

== Personal life ==
Zabolotoskaya Married to Yurii (Yura) Anatolevich Ilinskii in 1963, after they met at Moscow State University.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Summer2020 |url=https://acousticstoday.org/issues/2020AT/Summer2020/files/basic-html/page87.html |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=acousticstoday.org}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Zabolotskaya won the [[USSR State Prize]] in 1985. She is the 2017 winner of the [[ASA Silver Medal|Silver Medal]] in Physical Acoustics of the [[Acoustical Society of America]].{{r|silver}}

She was honored by the Women in Acoustics Committee of the Acoustical Society of America<ref>{{Cite web|title=2019 Fall Luncheon Honoree|url=https://womeninacoustics.org/2019-fall-luncheon-honoree/|access-date=2021-11-28|website=Women In Acoustics|language=en-US}}</ref> shortly before her death and highlighted in an [https://acousticstoday.org/work-parenting-harmony-tracianne-b-neilsen/ article on work-parenting harmony.]
